newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila call loan rate steady on lack of factors.
newsitem.headline: Manila call loan rate steady on lack of factors.

text.p: Philippine interbank call loan rates were steady at an average of 10.28125 percent on Wednesday after the Central Bank kept its rates at the same levels, traders said.
On Tuesday, the Central Bank dropped its overnight borrowing and lending rates by 0.1875 percentage points each to 10.25 and 12.75 percent, respectively.
"There's nothing to affect the market," a dealer said.
Done rates were in a range from 10.625 to 10.28125 percent with 29 lenders and 22 borrowers.
However, the Central Bank's offering of 91-day T-bills at 10.0 percent and 364-day bills at 10.7 percent spurred banks to give lower quotes on bills in the secondary market.
Banks saw active buying of T-bills as most institutions are swamped with high liquidity because they have shied away from term reverse repos which have a 20 percent tax, dealers said.
A Reuter poll of seven financial institutions gave bid rates of 10.025 to 10.175 percent for three-month bills, 10.30 to 10.40 for six months, and 10.76 to 10.875 for one year.
